newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium arrests Philips' Super Club founder.
newsitem.headline: Belgium arrests Philips' Super Club founder.

text.p: Belgian police have arrested the founder of the Super Club video rental business which Dutch company Philips Electronics NV took over in 1992, a public prosecutor's office spokesman said on Tuesday.

He said Belgian Maurits De Prins had been charged by examining magistrate Tony Heeren with fraud at the expense of former Belgian coalmining group Kempense Steenkoolmijnen (KS), forgery and use of forged documents.
Philips was not involved in this dossier, he said. De Prins was not available for comment.

KS bought 900,000 Super Club shares for 1.35 billion Belgian francs ($38.6 million) in November 1989. Super Club, which sells pre-recorded video cassettes, compact discs and computer games, subsequently collapsed and the share became virtually worthless.
The spokesman declined to say whether other people faced arrest.
He said the case hinged on a share buyback guarantee at a fixed price, offered by De Prins to KS.
Heeren sent investigators to the United States, Luxembourg and Britain in connection with the case, the spokesman said. De Prins mainly resides in the U.S. and Luxembourg.
Philips took control of Super Club in 1992 and sold its U.S. stores -- which accounted for 75 percent of total sales -- to video rental company Blockbuster Entertainment for $150 million in 1993.
The company announced in January it was also closing about 90 Super Club stores in Belgium, the Netherlands and France from April 1.
